text: Anthropic, the company behind Claude, has filed to go public. Its S-1
content:
Anthropic, the company behind Claude, has filed to go public. Its S-1 went to the SEC on 26 October, for Class A shares on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The share count and price range are not set yet.

What the filing shows (Anthropic S-1):

Revenue of $16.3 billion in the six months to June, against $4.6 billion in all of 2025.

A net loss of $80.7 billion over the same six months, of which $72.4 billion came from changes in the fair value of convertible notes and similar financing instruments.

Operating income of $974 million in the second quarter.

Customers paying $100,000 or more a year: about 20 at the end of 2023, more than 11,900 by 30 September 2026.

The filing also warns that advanced AI could "pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity", and says a trust and the founders are expected to elect the whole board.

Reports say the listing could value Anthropic at more than $2 trillion (NBC News). That figure is not in the filing. In June, Michael Burry said Anthropic might never be worth $1 trillion (Business Insider).

Sources: Anthropic, Anthropic S-1 (SEC), Yahoo Finance, NBC News, Business Insider. Video: Yahoo Finance. Photo: TechCrunch, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

When borrowing costs change, they reach almost every market, tech stocks included.

text: Mark Cuban sold Broadcast.com to Yahoo in 1999 for $5.7 billion in sto
content:
Mark Cuban sold Broadcast.com to Yahoo in 1999 for $5.7 billion in stock. Instead of riding the dot-com bubble higher, he hedged his Yahoo shares to protect what he had.

"How much money do I need?"

When the bubble burst, Yahoo's stock fell more than 90% from its peak.

Knowing when you have enough is a risk decision too. Would you have held on?

text: Elon Musk calls Tesla's new Roadster a flying car. Here is what it act
content:
Elon Musk calls Tesla's new Roadster a flying car. Here is what it actually did at the unveiling on 15 October.

At a SpaceX test site in Texas, the car used suction to climb a curved ramp and hang upside down, then dropped off, flipped and landed using air jets fed by high-pressure air tanks (CNN).

No one was inside. Musk said that was "to make sure we don't kill anyone."

Tesla claims 0 to 60 mph in under a second and says production starts in 2028. Neither has been independently verified, and Musk has missed past timelines.

"We're not talking about sustained flight," said Roger Connor of the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum (CNN).

Video: Tesla via X. Source: CNN.

content:
On 16 September 1992, Black Wednesday, the UK pulled the pound out of the European Exchange Rate Mechanism after failing to defend it.

George Soros's Quantum Fund had bet heavily against the pound and was reported to have made about $1 billion.

Few traders get a setup like that, and big bets can go badly wrong just as fast. Know the full size of your downside before you open any position.

text: 29 October 2025. The Fed had just cut rates, and markets saw another c
content:
29 October 2025. The Fed had just cut rates, and markets saw another cut in December as close to certain, with nearly 90 percent odds on CME FedWatch.

Then Jerome Powell said a December cut was "not a foregone conclusion, far from it." Within the press conference the odds slid to about 60 percent (CME FedWatch, via Kpler).

The Fed did cut again on 10 December 2025, to 3.50 to 3.75 percent, in a 9 to 3 vote (Federal Reserve, Reuters). Priced in is not the same as decided.

text: Gold closed at $3,898.90 an ounce on 30 October, below $4,000 and 26.7
content:
Gold closed at $3,898.90 an ounce on 30 October, below $4,000 and 26.7% under its record close of $5,318.40 in January (COMEX gold futures, Yahoo Finance).

That is in line with Bank of America's latest view. In a note published on 12 October, its analysts said they "remain cautious near-term" and expect gold to be unable to hold above $4,000 over the next three months (Kitco News).

Their fourth-quarter forecast is a $4,000 average, with a risk of dips toward $3,750 (investingLive, on BofA's 30 September outlook). The biggest threat they flag is an oil spike tied to the Iran war, and they note that central banks, China and India have slowed their gold buying.

It is not a long-term bearish call: BofA still expects gold to average $4,813 in 2027. Goldman Sachs is more upbeat, with a $5,400 target for end-2027 (investingLive, 23 September).

Sources: Kitco News, investingLive, Yahoo Finance. Photo: Stevebidmead via Pixabay, CC0, Wikimedia Commons.

He said guidance in 2021 "might well have slowed the policy response to high inflation."

Less guidance can mean bigger market moves on data days, because less is priced in ahead of time. Three weeks later the Fed raised rates (Federal Reserve, 16 Sep 2026).

text: The Fed has one main lever, the federal funds rate, which is the rate
content:
The Fed has one main lever, the federal funds rate, which is the rate for overnight borrowing between banks.

Lower it, and borrowing gets cheaper and asset prices tend to get a lift. Raise it, and borrowing costs rise across the economy.

That is why traders watch every FOMC meeting. The next one is on 8 and 9 December 2026.

text: 2 April 2025, the White House Rose Garden. President Trump held up a c
content:
2 April 2025, the White House Rose Garden. President Trump held up a chart of "reciprocal" tariffs, including 34 percent on China and a 10 percent baseline on other countries.

Stocks fell hard. The S&P 500 lost more than 10 percent from 2 to 4 April. On 9 April most of the new tariffs were paused for 90 days, and the index jumped 9.5 percent that day, its biggest one-day gain since 2008 (AP, Russell Investments).

Policy headlines can move markets fast in both directions. Gaps and slippage are real risks in weeks like that.

text: In 1982 Ray Dalio publicly predicted a depression. It turned out to be
content:
In 1982 Ray Dalio publicly predicted a depression. It turned out to be close to the exact bottom of the stock market.

He lost money for himself and his clients, let his staff go, and borrowed $4,000 from his dad to pay family bills.

He calls it one of the best things that ever happened to him, because it changed how he makes decisions. He went on to build Bridgewater Associates.

text: Myth #01: lose 50%, then gain 50%, and you're back to even.Fact: you n
content:
Myth #01: lose 50%, then gain 50%, and you're back to even.

Fact: you need a 100% gain to recover.

Hypothetical example: start with $1,000. Lose 50% and you have $500. A 50% gain on $500 only gets you to $750. To get back to $1,000, you need +100%.

The bigger the loss, the steeper the climb: -10% needs +11%, -25% needs +33%, -50% needs +100%, -75% needs +300%.

Protect your capital first. Which trading myth should we bust next?
